ECE 6390 / Digital signals

Quantization & PCM

From the figure to the physics

Fig. 1 shows how sample rate and amplitude levels determine a raw digital representation.

Sampling chooses observation times; quantization assigns each amplitude to one of L = 2ᵇ levels. Raw PCM bit rate is fsb before framing, compression, or channel coding.

State the quantizer convention. For L equally spaced reconstruction levels including both endpoints of a voltage range, adjacent-level spacing is Δ = (Vmax − Vmin)/(L − 1). An equal-width-bin convention has a different denominator.

The familiar SQNR estimate 6.02b + 1.76 dB assumes a high-resolution full-scale sinusoid and an approximately uniform quantization-error model. Clipping and a lower signal amplitude change the result.

Example

A four-bit endpoint-level quantizer spanning −1 to +1 V has 16 levels spaced by 2/15 ≈ 0.133 V. At 8,000 samples/s, its raw PCM rate is 32 kbit/s.

    1. At 48,000 samples/s and 12 bits per sample, what is the raw mono PCM bit rate? Which overheads have been omitted?

    Multiply samples per second by bits per sample.

    576,000 bit/s, or 576 kbit/s. Framing, metadata, channel coding, and any additional channels are outside this raw-rate calculation.
